questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: We eat the seeds of which of these plants?
questions.explanation: Wheat grains are seeds. Spinach is a leaf, carrot a root and cauliflower a flower.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of these animals is kept to get milk?
questions.explanation: Buffaloes, like cows and goats, give milk.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which pair has one stem and one leaf used as food?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane is a stem and spinach is a leaf.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of the following animals is a carnivore?
questions.explanation: An eagle feeds on other animals.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: A child's lunch has roti, a banana and a glass of milk. Which choice names the source of each item correctly?
options: Roti from a seed (grain), banana from a fruit, milk from an animal
Roti from an animal, banana from a root, milk from a leaf
Roti from a seed, banana from a stem, milk from a plant
Roti from a flower, banana from an animal, milk from honey
questions.explanation: Roti is made from wheat grain, a banana is a fruit and milk comes from animals.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Which of these foods is obtained from a plant seed and is rich in protein?
questions.explanation: Chickpeas are seeds of a pulse crop and contain a lot of protein.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Why is milk an important food for growing children?
questions.answer: Milk contains proteins for growth, calcium for bones and teeth, and other nutrients and water.
questions.explanation: Milk is a nutritious food.

questions.topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
questions.q: Why is it better for a person to eat a variety of foods than only one kind of food?
questions.answer: Different foods give different nutrients. A single food cannot give all the nutrients in the right amounts, so variety keeps the diet balanced.
questions.explanation: A balanced diet needs variety.

questions.q: Which nutrient do rice and potatoes mainly provide?
questions.explanation: Rice and potatoes are rich in starch, a carbohydrate.

questions.q: Which of these is rich in vitamin C?
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits such as oranges and lemons are rich in vitamin C.

questions.q: Which food is the best source of calcium?
questions.explanation: Milk and milk products contain a lot of calcium.

questions.q: Carrots and papaya help the eyes because they contain
questions.explanation: Many orange and yellow fruits and vegetables give vitamin A.

questions.q: A girl eats plenty of pulses and green leafy vegetables but is often tired and pale. A doctor finds anaemia. Which addition would help most?
options: Foods rich in iron, such as leafy vegetables and jaggery taken regularly
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in the blood, so iron-rich foods help.

questions.q: Which of the following does a balanced diet NOT need?
options: Large amounts of only one nutrient
questions.explanation: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in suitable amounts, not one in excess.

questions.q: Write the functions of proteins and minerals in the body.
questions.answer: Proteins help in growth and repair of the body. Minerals keep the body healthy, for example calcium for bones and iron for blood.
questions.explanation: Each nutrient has its own role.

questions.q: A child eats mostly noodles and fried snacks. Which nutrients may be missing in the diet and what could be added?
questions.answer: Vitamins, minerals, proteins and roughage may be lacking. Fruits, vegetables, pulses and milk should be added.
questions.explanation: A balanced diet needs variety.

questions.q: Which of the following is a natural fibre?
questions.explanation: Cotton is obtained from a plant. Nylon, polyester and acrylic are made in factories.

questions.q: Wool is obtained from the hair of
options: Animals such as sheep and goat
questions.explanation: Hair from sheep, goat, yak and similar animals gives wool.

questions.q: Which step comes first in making cloth?
questions.explanation: Fibres are first spun into yarn, which is later woven into cloth.

questions.q: Which of these statements about silk is right?
options: It comes from the cocoon of a silkworm
questions.explanation: Silk fibre is produced by silkworms.

questions.q: A farmer in a region with black soil and warm weather wants a plant fibre crop. Which crop suits the place best?
questions.explanation: Cotton grows well in black soil and warm weather.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a fibre obtained from plants?
questions.explanation: Wool comes from animals.

questions.q: Write two differences between weaving and knitting.
questions.answer: Weaving uses two sets of yarn crossing at right angles and is done on a loom. Knitting uses a single yarn with needles.
keyPoints: Weaving: two sets of yarn at right angles
questions.explanation: Both turn yarn into fabric.

questions.q: A person wants a warm jacket for a cold place. Which fibre will you suggest and why?
questions.answer: Wool, because the woollen fibres trap air which is a poor conductor of heat, keeping the body warm.
questions.explanation: The fibre is chosen according to its properties.

questions.q: Which of these is made of metal?
questions.explanation: Steel is an alloy made mostly of iron, a metal.

questions.q: The materials that do not allow us to see through them are
questions.explanation: Opaque materials stop light.

questions.q: Which of these is insoluble in water?
questions.explanation: Sand does not dissolve in water.

questions.q: A wooden block floats, but an iron block of the same size sinks. This shows that
options: Iron is heavier for its size than water, and wood is lighter
Wood is heavier for its size than iron
questions.explanation: Iron is denser than water and wood is less dense.

questions.q: A student has a list: chalk, coin, glass bead, paper clip. She wants to separate metals. Which pair would she pick?
questions.explanation: Coins and paper clips are metallic and lustrous.

questions.q: Which of these shows that a substance is soluble in water?
options: It sinks to the bottom as particles
It disappears and spreads evenly in the water
It changes the colour of the beaker
questions.explanation: A dissolved substance spreads evenly and cannot be seen separately.

questions.q: Give two examples each of materials that are hard and soft.
questions.answer: Hard: iron, stone. Soft: cotton wool, sponge.
questions.explanation: Hardness is a property we can test by pressing or scratching.

questions.q: A cup of tea is stirred with a metal spoon and the handle becomes warm. Explain using a property of metals.
questions.answer: Metals allow heat to pass through them easily, so heat travels along the spoon from the hot tea to the handle.
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat.

questions.q: Which method is used to get salt from sea water?
questions.explanation: Water evaporates in the sun and leaves salt.

questions.q: Separating grains from the stalks of harvested crops is
questions.explanation: Threshing beats the stalks to remove the grains.

questions.q: A tea strainer is similar to which method of separation?
questions.explanation: Liquid passes through the holes and tea leaves are left behind.

questions.q: Which method separates iron nails from a mixture of nails and sawdust quickly?
questions.explanation: The magnet attracts the iron.

questions.q: Salt is dissolved in water in a pan which is then heated until the water is gone. What is left behind?
questions.explanation: Water evaporates but the salt remains.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a method of separating mixtures?
questions.explanation: Rusting is a chemical change, not a separation method.

questions.q: How does a farmer separate wheat grains from the husk?
questions.answer: By winnowing: the mixture is dropped from a height in the wind, so lighter husk blows away and grains fall in a heap.
questions.explanation: Weight difference allows separation.

questions.q: Why can't we use a sieve to separate salt from salt water but can use evaporation?
questions.answer: Dissolved salt particles are too small and pass through any sieve. Heating evaporates the water and leaves the salt.
questions.explanation: The method depends on the properties of the mixture.

questions.q: The change of water vapour to liquid water is
questions.explanation: Cooling water vapour turns it into liquid.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a reversible change?
options: Stretching and releasing a rubber band
questions.explanation: A rubber band regains shape when released.

questions.q: Which change is irreversible?
questions.explanation: Cooked vegetables cannot be turned back to raw.

questions.q: Which change is caused by cooling?
questions.explanation: Water freezes when cooled.

questions.q: A wet iron nail is left in the open for a week and becomes covered by a reddish-brown layer. Which statement is correct?
options: The nail has undergone a reversible change
The nail has undergone rusting, which is an irreversible change
questions.explanation: Rusting forms a new substance and cannot be reversed.

questions.q: Which of these is a natural change?
questions.explanation: Day and night are natural changes that no one controls.

questions.q: List two ways to prevent rusting of iron articles.
questions.answer: Painting the iron or coating it with oil or grease keeps air and water away, preventing rust.
questions.explanation: Rust needs air and water.

questions.q: Why are the changes of a baked cake irreversible while melting of ice is reversible?
questions.answer: Baking forms new substances with new properties that cannot be turned back, but melting is only a change of state and the water can be frozen again.
questions.explanation: Reversibility depends on whether new substances form.

questions.q: Plants that have a hard, thick stem and many branches high above the ground are called
questions.explanation: Trees are tall with a woody trunk.

questions.q: The green colour of leaves is due to
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that traps sunlight.

questions.q: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit?
questions.explanation: The ovary grows into the fruit.

questions.q: Plants with tap roots usually have leaves with
questions.explanation: Tap roots go with reticulate (net-like) venation.

questions.q: A gardener cuts all the roots of a small plant before planting it. The plant is likely to
options: Wilt because it cannot take water from the soil
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals, so without them the plant wilts.

questions.q: The male reproductive part of a flower is the
questions.explanation: The stamen produces pollen.

questions.q: What are the functions of the stem?
questions.answer: The stem supports the plant, carries water and minerals from roots to leaves and carries food from leaves to other parts.
questions.explanation: The stem connects all parts.

questions.q: Explain why most plants die if kept in dark for a long time.
questions.answer: Photosynthesis needs sunlight, so in the dark leaves cannot make food and the plant slowly starves.
questions.explanation: Light is essential for food making in green plants.

questions.q: Bones are joined to muscles. When muscles contract they
options: Pull the bones and cause movement
questions.explanation: Muscles pull on bones to move them.

questions.q: Which of these protects the spinal cord?
questions.explanation: The spinal cord runs inside the backbone.

questions.q: A person turning the head to look sideways uses
questions.explanation: The neck has a pivotal joint.

questions.q: An earthworm has no bones. It moves with the help of
questions.explanation: Muscles and tiny bristles grip the soil.

questions.q: Which statement correctly explains why we can swing our arms in circles but cannot rotate our knees in the same way?
options: The shoulder is a ball and socket joint, the knee is a hinge joint
questions.explanation: A ball and socket joint allows rotation, while a hinge joint allows movement in one direction.

questions.q: Which bones form the rib cage along with the chest bone?
questions.explanation: Ribs are curved bones that join the chest bone and the backbone.

questions.q: Why do birds have light bones, and how does the shape of a fish help it to swim?
questions.answer: Light bones make a bird's body light for flying. The streamlined shape of a fish reduces resistance of water.
questions.explanation: Body structure suits the way of moving.

questions.q: What would happen if there were no muscles attached to our bones?
questions.answer: The bones could not be moved, so we could not walk, lift or bend, since muscles pull on bones.
questions.explanation: Movement needs both bones and muscles.

questions.q: Which of these needs food to live?
questions.explanation: Plants make their own food, but all living things need food.

questions.q: The surroundings in which a plant or animal lives is its
questions.explanation: A habitat is the home of an organism.

questions.q: Which of the following is a land (terrestrial) habitat?
questions.explanation: Forests are on land.

questions.q: Which feature helps a bird fly?
questions.explanation: Wings and feathers help birds to fly.

questions.q: Why do the leaves of many desert plants look small or spiny?
questions.explanation: Smaller leaves lose less water by transpiration.

questions.q: The process of getting rid of waste by living organisms is called
questions.explanation: Excretion removes waste from the body.

questions.q: Write any three differences between living and non-living things.
questions.answer: Living things grow, breathe, need food and reproduce, while non-living things do not.
questions.explanation: These are signs of life.

questions.q: Why are some animals active at night in the desert?
questions.answer: The days are very hot, so staying hidden in the day and coming out at night helps them save water and avoid heat.
questions.explanation: This is a habit that helps survival.

questions.q: The SI unit of length is the
questions.explanation: The metre is the SI unit of length.

questions.q: The to-and-fro motion of a swing is
questions.explanation: It repeats after equal intervals.

questions.q: The length of a straight line is best measured by
questions.explanation: Metre scales measure length.

questions.q: The hands of a clock move in
questions.explanation: The hands turn in circles about the centre.

questions.q: The length of a wire is 2 m 30 cm. What is its length in centimetres?
The metre scale has markings in
questions.explanation: A ruler is marked in centimetres and millimetres.

questions.q: Why should the eye be placed directly above the mark while reading a ruler?
questions.answer: Reading from the side gives a wrong value due to the slanted line of sight, so we must look straight at the mark.
questions.explanation: This avoids reading error.

questions.q: A bus travels 36 km in a trip. Express the distance in metres and explain which unit is more convenient.
questions.answer: 36 x 1000 = 36000 m. Kilometre is more convenient since the number is smaller for long distances.
questions.explanation: Choose a unit that suits the size.

questions.q: Which of these can form a shadow?
questions.explanation: An opaque object blocks light to form a shadow.

questions.q: Which of the following is a natural source of light?
questions.explanation: The Sun is natural; the others are man-made.

questions.q: In which case will the shadow of a ball be the biggest?
options: Ball far from lamp, near screen
Ball near lamp, far from screen
questions.explanation: The closer to the light and farther from the screen, the larger the shadow.

questions.q: The image in a pinhole camera is formed on a
questions.explanation: A translucent screen allows the image to be seen.

questions.q: A person stands 1 m in front of a plane mirror. Her image seems to be behind the mirror at about
questions.explanation: The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.q: Which of the following can be seen only by reflected light?
questions.explanation: The Moon reflects the Sun's light.

questions.q: Why do we use mirrors and not wooden boards for seeing ourselves?
questions.answer: A mirror has a smooth shiny surface that reflects most light to form a clear image, but wood is rough and scatters light.
keyPoints: Wood does not form clear image
questions.explanation: Smooth polished surfaces give images.

questions.q: Explain why you see an upside-down image on a pinhole camera screen.
questions.answer: Light travels in straight lines, so rays from the top of the object go downward through the hole and rays from the bottom go upward, inverting the image.
questions.explanation: The crossing of rays inverts the image.

questions.q: A smooth shiny surface that reflects well is called a
questions.explanation: Mirrors reflect light to give images.

questions.q: An object that lights up when current passes through its filament is a
questions.explanation: The filament glows when current passes.

questions.q: The material used to cover electric wires is
questions.explanation: Plastic is an insulator.

questions.q: Which of the following will light a bulb in a circuit tester?
questions.explanation: The iron key is a conductor.

questions.q: Which part of the circuit lets us put the bulb on or off?
questions.explanation: A switch controls the circuit.

questions.q: A student connects a bulb to a cell with wires, but one wire end is not touching the cell. What will happen?
options: The bulb does not light as the circuit is incomplete
questions.explanation: Without contact the circuit is open.

questions.q: A bulb has how many terminals?
questions.explanation: A bulb has two terminals.

questions.q: Why does electricity pass through copper but not through plastic?
questions.answer: Copper is a metal and conducts electricity, while plastic is an insulator.
questions.explanation: Metals are good conductors.

questions.q: Why are tools like screwdrivers for electricians given insulated plastic handles?
questions.answer: Plastic is an insulator, so it prevents current passing to the electrician's hand and avoids shocks.
questions.explanation: Safety around live wires.

questions.q: Pure rubber, glass and dry wood are examples of
questions.explanation: They do not allow current to pass.

questions.q: The north pole of a magnet will attract the
questions.explanation: Unlike poles attract.

questions.q: Which of the following materials is magnetic?
questions.explanation: Nickel is magnetic.

questions.q: A compass needle is a
questions.explanation: It is a small magnetised needle.

questions.q: Which of these shows the safe way to store magnets?
options: Keep unlike poles together with a piece of wood between pairs
questions.explanation: This helps them keep their strength.

questions.q: A child finds that a strong magnet picks up steel pins but not aluminium foil. What is the best conclusion?
options: Steel is a magnetic material but aluminium is not
questions.explanation: Steel contains iron which is magnetic, while aluminium is non-magnetic.

questions.q: Iron filings are most attracted to the
questions.explanation: The attraction is strongest at the poles.

questions.q: What is a compass and how does it help in finding directions?
questions.answer: A compass has a magnetic needle that rests in the north-south direction, which lets us find north and other directions.
questions.explanation: It is used for navigation.

questions.q: Why should magnets be kept away from televisions, mobile phones and credit cards? Give a reason.
questions.answer: Strong magnets can damage the magnetic parts in such devices and cards, so they should be kept away.
questions.explanation: A common safety precaution.
